e7_s4_rationale: The patient's history of hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use suggests immunocompromised status, and the presence of progressive neurological deficits, leukocytosis, and pleocytosis in the cerebrospinal fluid, along with the characteristic MRI findings of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the basal ganglia and internal capsule, are consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy

e7_s4_rejected.label: CNS Lymphoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Lack of enhancement after gadolinium on MRI makes CNS Lymphoma less likely

e7_s4_rejected.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple ring-enhancing lesions on MRI, which are not described in this case

e7_s4_rejected.label: Brain Abscess
e7_s4_rejected.why: Would typically present with more pronounced mass effect, enhancement on MRI, and a more acute clinical course

e7_s4_rejected.label: CNS Tuberculosis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Typically presents with more pronounced meningeal signs, and the CSF profile does not strongly suggest tuberculosis
